earlier_scan.note: Extinct Cariban variety; Glottolog lists only 19th/early-20th c. wordlists (Schomburgk 1849, Martius 1867, Farabee 1924, Koch-Grünberg 1928) and Girard 1971 comparative work; no descriptive phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog languoid page wayu1242 and its 5 reference records (Koch-Grünberg 1928 wordlist pp. 257-272; Schomburgk 1849; Farabee 1924; Martius 1867; Girard 1971).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; confirms extinct (AES 10), zero grammar/phonology/sketch references.

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2006. A família lingüística Caribe (Karíb). Revista de Estudos e Pesquisas (FUNAI, Brasília) 3(1/2): 157-174.
sources.note: Mentioned once, with Sapará, as an extinct Cariban language recorded by Koch-Grünberg 'na área entre Roraima e o Orinoco'; the family-level phonology overview does not refer to it; nothing on Wayumará stress. (Boanarí/Bonari does not occur in the article.)
sources.venue: Revista de Estudos e Pesquisas (FUNAI, Brasília)

sources.citation: Gildea, Spike. 2003. Proposing a new branch for the Cariban language family. Amerindia 28: 7-32.
sources.note: Listed only inside Kaufman's classification table; no Wayumara data; same general remark (p. 10) that early sources cannot reliably indicate stress.

sources.citation: Durbin, Marshall. 1977. A survey of the Carib language family. In: Ellen B. Basso (ed.), Carib-Speaking Indians: Culture, Society and Language (Anthropological Papers of the University of Arizona 28), 23-38. Tucson: University of Arizona Press. (Open-access web edition 2022, Manifold, chapter 2.)
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for any language (a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|tone|tonal = 0 in the chapter). The only linguistic content bearing on Wayumara is diachronic-segmental: 'The third linguistic subdivision we have chosen to call Southern Guiana Carib. It consists, on the one hand, of Kashuyana, Warikyana, Kahuyana, and Ingarune (all dialects of the same language), and, on the other, of Hishkaryana, Wayumara-Azumara, Parukoto, and Ye'cuana. In these languages several sound shifts have taken place, the most prominent of which is the change of Proto-Carib *p to Proto…
sources.venue: Anthropological Papers of the University of Arizona 28

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages (ed. Johannes Wilbert). Los Angeles: Latin American Center, UCLA. 453 pp.
sources.note: 'Wayumara or Azumara or Guimara - spoken between the Mucajai and Uraricoera Rivers and in a part of Maraca Island. [Farabee 1924, pp. 243-245; Koch-Grunberg 1913, p. 455, 1928, pp. 258-272.]' Location and sources only; no phonetic or prosodic remark.

sources.citation: Shafer, Robert. 1963. Vergleichende Phonetik der karaibischen Sprachen. Verhandelingen der Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen, Afd. Letterkunde, N.R. 69(2). Amsterdam: Noord-Hollandsche Uitgevers Maatschappij. 76 pp. (cites c. 65 Wayumara forms from Koch-Grünberg 1928 and c. 5 Azumara forms from Farabee 1924 in its correspondence sets).
sources.note: Segmental sound correspondences only. The word 'Akzent' occurs twice in the monograph and neither passage concerns Wayumara: p. 44 'Die stärkste phonetische Veränderung.. ist der Schwund der letzten Silbe einiger Wörter in gewissen Sprachen der apoto-Gruppe. Weder Akzent noch die phonetische Umgebung ist der Grund davon' (Kamarakoto/Arekuna/Taulipang/Purukoto/Akawai), and 'Akzent auf letzter Sylbe, wenn nicht -una' appended to the Uiraboy (Patagona/Paraviyana) word lists. Nothing on Wayumara accent or tone.
sources.venue: Verhandelingen der Koninklijke Nederlandse Akademie van Wetenschappen, Afd

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1928. Vom Roroima zum Orinoco, Bd. IV: Sprachen (ed. F. Hestermann). Stuttgart: Strecker und Schröder. Section 'Sapará, Purukotó, Wayumará', pp. 257-272 ('Das Wayumará' p. 258; Wayumará = third column of the comparative wordlist); transcription key pp. 2-3.
sources.note: Silent. The p. 258 intro is purely classificatory (p>h lenition; link between Yapurá Caribs and Trio/Galibi); the volume's transcription key (pp. 2-3, Anthropos alphabet) covers vowel/consonant values and length but states no stress rule. Wayumará forms carry acute accents, mostly on the final syllable (p. 258: inú, yebí, yona:lí, yenu:rú, ihubé, motalé; but ye:nužípo, ihetámužipo) — raw data, not a stated rule.

sources.citation: Farabee, William Curtis. 1924. The Central Caribs. University of Pennsylvania, University Museum Anthropological Publications vol. X. Philadelphia. 'Azumaras' pp. 242-245 (English–Azumara vocabulary and numerals); phonetic key p. 97.
sources.note: Silent. Vocabulary from two brothers met on the Maraca River, sporadic acute accents on forms; the phonetic key (p. 97) says nothing about accent.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1893. Matériaux pour servir à l'établissement d'une grammaire comparée des dialectes de la famille Caribe. (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine, tome XVII.) Paris: J. Maisonneuve. (Waiyamara = one of the compared dialects, abbreviation 'Waiy.', data from Schomburgk 1848; Partie grammaticale e.g. 1sg index i- 'i-pawa ma tête'; Partie lexiologique passim.)
sources.note: The only phonological section, 'Accidents phonétiques' at the head of the Partie lexiologique, covers aphérèse, syncope, apocope and métathèse of vowels and consonants across the dialects; there is no paragraph on accent, and the words accent/tonique/prononciation do not occur in the volume. Waiyamara forms are cited without accent marks (Schomburgk's orthography). Silent on stress and tone for Wayumará (and for the family).
sources.venue: (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine, tome XVII.) Paris: J

sources.citation: Steinen, Karl von den. 1892. Die Bakaïrí-Sprache: Wörterverzeichnis, Sätze, Sagen, Grammatik. Mit Beiträgen zu einer Lautlehre der karaïbischen Grundsprache. Leipzig: K. F. Koehler's Antiquarium. (Part II 'Lautlehre der karaibischen Grundsprache': source list 'WAIYAMARA R. Schomburgk vgl. akawai b'; c. 10 Wayamara forms from Schomburgk 1848 cited in the comparative notes, e.g. 'Wayamara yonari' under kχanari 'Nase', 'Wayamara okheri Hund'.)
sources.note: Nothing for Wayumara. Every Accent/betont passage concerns Bakairi (sec. 320 'Accent', djvu l. 41472 'Der Accent ruht durchgängig auf der vorletzten Silbe'; the Eigennamen note on bakairí vs bakáiri, l. 9240-9248) or is an etymological aside not tied to a language ('Accent fast nur auf der letzten Silbe' for the 'Mandioka' reflexes, l. 6331). The section 'Lautliche Unsicherheit' (pp. 249 f., l. 35360 ff.) discusses the unreliability of the old travellers' transcriptions in general. Wayamara forms are Schomburgk's, printed without accent marks.
sources.venue: Mit Beiträgen zu einer Lautlehre der karaïbischen Grundsprache

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867 [1863]. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II: Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. 'Vocabula comparata e dialectis Guyanae britanicae' pp. 312-313.
sources.note: Silent. Reprints Schomburgk's 1848 comparative table (incl. Waiyamara); no remarks on pronunciation beyond Schomburgk's.
sources.venue: Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd

sources.note: Silent. 'Waiyamara' is no. 5 of his Caribi-Tamanakan section; 18-word comparative table; orthography note (p. 97) gives Italian vowel values and consonant conventions only.
